newsitem.title: CANADA: Finning still sees Leverton boosting net.
newsitem.headline: Finning still sees Leverton boosting net.

text.p: Heavy equipment dealer Finning Ltd said on Monday it still expected its proposed acquisition of H Leverton Ltd from Unilever Plc to boost 1997 earnings even if the deal took more time to close.
Finning said in August it was in talks with Unilever to acquire Leverton, which holds a Caterpillar Inc franchise in Britain. Finning hoped the deal would close in the first quarter.
Finning chief financial officer Rick Mahler was asked in a conference call if the acquisition would still be accretive to earnings if hypothetically it did not close until May.
"We believe it can be," he said, adding, "We don't think there are any substantive costs involved in the acquisition and we think that we can generate some profitability."

"Obviously the closer it happens toward year end -- and I'm not predicting that this is the case -- the tougher it would be for us to be accretive. But at this point in time, we're hopeful we'll be able to conclude something fairly soon," Mahler said. The talks with Unilever are covered by a confidentiality agreement.
Finning in reporting fourth-quarter earnings today today said the talks were proceeding but gave no more details.
Asked if a May closing was now being mooted, Mahler said that was the first time he had heard the date discussed.
Finning said there would be costs associated with the acquisition but that they would mostly be accounted for as goodwill rather than restructuring charges to earnings.
Under the proposed Leverton deal, Finning would sell its Caterpillar dealership in Poland and its U.K. finance portfolio. Proceeds would finance the acquisition.

Analysts have estimated Finning would pay about C$200 million for Leverton. They projected the acquisition would initially add about C$0.50 a share to Finning's annual earnings and a further C$0.10 a share when the operations were fully integrated over the next two the three years.
